It is assumed that the low median is affecting the sale of services and goods in the City and in the area. To what extent this impact exists is not clear, for the general economy of the City appears to be good as indicated by the list of sales recorded in the City of Harrisburg for the year 1972:

It should be noted that some of the above sales for the year 1972 may have been inflated as a result of the replacement of household items destroyed by the 1972 Flood. Funds to purchase many of these items may have been derived from loans and grants made available through the Small Business Administration's disaster relief program.
It was observed, during the development of this report, that the downtown areas (CBD) of Harrisburg appeared to be experiencing general prosperity in retail sales. However, a few stores did not reopen after the flood. The outlying areas, also, appeared to be experiencing similar prosperity. To what extent Federal funding of disaster programs in the area has helped to bolster the local economy has not been determined; however, it is believed to have stabilized the situation somewhat.
i. Racial Characteristics
The percentage of non-white population in the City of Harrisburg, 30.7 percent, is much greater than that of the total SMSA's 6.8 percent. Minorities, other than negro or white, account for approximately one-half of one percent of the total population. (See Table 13).
